discovery_status: Brief-only discovery; exact plan withheld until the required one-time helper release.

sources.title: RFC 4180 — Common Format and MIME Type for CSV Files
sources.locator: §2 items 3–7 and ABNF; optional header, comma-separated fields, equal field counts, spaces are data, quoted embedded CR/LF/comma/quote.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC and inspected the format definition.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The described common format uses comma delimiters; headers are optional and should be signaled; quoted fields may contain commas and line breaks; spaces are significant. RFC explicitly says it is informational, not an Internet Standard.
sources.applicability: Baseline for record boundaries and why physical lines do not equal logical records; supplier variations require explicit dialect profiles.
sources.evidence_limitations: Informational 2005 description; not evidence that every supplier follows RFC 4180.

sources.title: W3C Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
sources.locator: Dialect Description and default dialect (§5.9); tableSchema / columns examples including titles, datatype/format, required and primaryKey.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the dated W3C Recommendation and searched dialect/schema properties.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default description identifies UTF-8, CRLF/LF, quote character, doubleQuote, header, comma delimiter, and whitespace behavior; descriptions may override these. Column metadata can carry titles, datatypes/formats and constraints.
sources.applicability: Useful model for a versioned local supplier profile combining dialect and column mapping; adopt only a documented subset. Its table primaryKey is file-schema metadata and does not make supplier codes globally unique in the stock domain.
sources.evidence_limitations: Web-oriented metadata model; does not prescribe the application's matching, duplicate, inventory, transaction, or UX policy.

sources.title: Rust csv 1.4.0 ReaderBuilder API
sources.locator: ReaderBuilder methods delimiter, has_headers, flexible, quote, escape, double_quote; record iteration and reusable read_record examples.
sources.observed_operation: Opened docs.rs 1.4.0 API reference and inspected configuration defaults and iteration examples.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Delimiter defaults to comma, header handling defaults on, and unequal record field counts error by default; flexible(true) disables that count check. Quote is double quote by default; non-doubled backslash-style escapes are disabled unless configured.
sources.applicability: Concrete Rust parser option for streaming raw records under an explicit supplier profile; validate strictness and encoding behavior against app requirements.
sources.evidence_limitations: Library behavior only; no stock app repository or caller was provided.

sources.title: Rust csv 1.4.0 Position API
sources.locator: Position overview and byte(), line(), record() methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Each position contains byte offset, line number and record index; byte and record begin at 0, line begins at 1. Reader assigns record positions.
sources.applicability: Use a stable logical record number and byte offset for audit/review; display physical line as a convenience and test multiline and CRLF cases before relying on it.
sources.evidence_limitations: Does not define the product's displayed source-location convention or ensure every parser's line counting agrees.

sources.title: BurntSushi rust-csv reader source and inline tests
sources.release_or_commit: Git ref 1.4.0; crate release 1.4.0; commit SHA not separately resolved
sources.locator: ReaderBuilder::flexible (around line 300); ReaderState::add_record; #[cfg(test)] module and read_record_unequal_ok test (around lines 2097–2280).
sources.observed_operation: Opened and searched the tagged upstream source; inspected the unequal-length check and in-file tests.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: ReaderState compares later record width with the first parsed width when flexible is false and attaches the record position to UnequalLengths; flexible true bypasses this width error. Inline tests demonstrate the option.
sources.applicability: Source-level corroboration for strict width validation and row attribution; malformed rows should be classified for review, not made permissive by default.
sources.evidence_limitations: Upstream parser test/source, not tests for the stock application or supplier files.

sources.title: Python 3.14 csv module documentation
sources.locator: reader and DictReader; Dialect attributes; Sniffer; Reader Objects line_num.
sources.observed_operation: Opened Python 3.14 documentation and inspected string conversion, dialect, strict, and line_num behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reader yields strings unless QUOTE_NONNUMERIC is selected; Dialect.strict defaults false; line_num counts source lines and is not the number of records when fields span multiple lines. Sniffer infers a dialect from a supplied sample.
sources.applicability: Lightweight standard-library alternative and a useful comparison for row-level diagnostics; keep inference advisory and raw values textual.
sources.evidence_limitations: Language/runtime not specified for target app; behavior must be checked against the app's pinned runtime.

sources.title: CPython 3.14.8 csv implementation and tests
sources.locator: Lib/csv.py Sniffer.sniff and _guess_delimiter; Lib/test/test_csv.py test_read_linenum, test_roundtrip_quoteed_newlines, test_read_bigfield.
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged implementation and test files; inspected the Sniffer source and tests for line counts, embedded newlines, and large fields.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Sniffer chooses from a sample and prefers comma/tab/semicolon/space/colon on ties; tests show line_num increments by input lines and reader/writer round-trip quoted newlines; test_read_bigfield exercises 50,000-character fields.
sources.applicability: Repository-code evidence for a minimal parser option and useful test scenarios; illustrates sample-based inference and that physical-line counts are not logical record numbers.
sources.evidence_limitations: The selected CPython test file is not a test suite for this application and no tests were run during this research.

sources.title: DuckDB CSV Import documentation (preview)
sources.release_or_commit: Moving preview documentation; no immutable release or commit exposed by the page at access
sources.locator: CSV sniffer and configuration options, especially sample_size, strict_mode, all_varchar, decimal_separator, thousands, and rejects handling.
sources.observed_operation: Opened current preview docs via search result and inspected option/default summaries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The docs describe dialect, header, and type auto-detection; sample_size defaults to 20,480 rows; strict_mode defaults true; column types, decimal and thousands separators, and reject storage are configurable.
sources.applicability: Local SQL/query-engine alternative for exploratory profiling or a staging area; a sample below the brief's 80,000-row ceiling cannot by itself prove all-row structure, and type/dialect inference should not authorize stock changes.
sources.evidence_limitations: Preview docs are moving and not a version pin. Recheck exact behavior against the chosen release; no benchmark or test was run.

sources.title: DuckDB issue #25827 — dialect change can discard earlier rows
sources.release_or_commit: Issue opened 17 September 2026; open / needs-triage when accessed; no fix or release link observed
sources.locator: Issue description, minimal three-line reproduction, 30,000-row reproduction, discussion of sniff buffer and sample_size.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream issue, checked status, and inspected the report's reproduction and claimed option results.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter describes a file with changing row dialect/width where default sniffing treats early content as preamble; report claims sample_size=-1 does not fix that case, while null_padding=true retains rows but changes interpretation. It was still open at access.
sources.applicability: High-consequence warning against trusting auto-sniffed row counts or treating a larger sample as proof; require explicit schema, full-file reconciliation, and pinned-version regression tests if DuckDB is considered.
sources.evidence_limitations: This is an open user report, not independently reproduced here and not proof of behavior in every DuckDB release.

sources.title: BurntSushi rust-csv Discussion #402 — unequal field counts
sources.locator: Question on mismatched header/record widths and accepted maintainer answer.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the upstream discussion and read maintainer guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Maintainer explains that changing header names does not change record-width validation and that flexible parsing disables the unequal-length error.
sources.applicability: Reinforces S03/S05; do not enable permissive widths as a silent fix because the importer still needs to show the row as a schema/validation issue.
sources.evidence_limitations: Discussion answer, not release note or target-app behavior.

sources.title: SQLite Transactions
sources.release_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation; no immutable release version exposed
sources.locator: Transaction lifecycle, rollback, BEGIN DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE, SQLITE_BUSY condition.
sources.observed_operation: Opened transaction documentation and inspected write-start and busy behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately and can fail SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active; transaction/rollback semantics can provide a candidate atomic boundary.
sources.applicability: Conditional design option if the existing stock store is SQLite; keep the write transaction short and handle a busy conflict without partial application.
sources.evidence_limitations: Backend is unspecified; the proposal cannot assume SQLite semantics or transaction cost for 80,000 rows.

sources.title: SQLite UPSERT
sources.release_or_commit: SQLite UPSERT added in 3.24.0; generalized in 3.35.0; docs updated 2024-04-11
sources.locator: Conflict target and DO UPDATE semantics; §4 History.
sources.observed_operation: Opened documentation and inspected conflict-update semantics and version history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UPSERT chooses behavior on a uniqueness/primary-key conflict; DO UPDATE changes the conflicting row. Constraint violations in the DO UPDATE path abort the INSERT statement.
sources.applicability: Can support a unique import-batch/row ledger if SQLite is used; uniqueness keys must reflect supplier, file/profile and row identity, not a bare supplier product code.
sources.evidence_limitations: A database UPSERT alone does not define inventory snapshot-vs-delta semantics or make application logic idempotent.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 COPY
sources.locator: COPY FROM options ON_ERROR, REJECT_LIMIT, LOG_VERBOSITY, ENCODING; CSV NULL/header handling.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PostgreSQL 18 reference and inspected default error action and reject reporting options.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: COPY fails on processing errors by default; ON_ERROR can alter conversion-error behavior, and ignore may discard unlimited erroneous rows unless a REJECT_LIMIT is specified. Verbose mode can report input line and column for discarded conversion rows.
sources.applicability: Conditional server-database bulk-staging alternative. If used, land raw data in a private staging table and preserve rejected-row detail; don't use ignore as a substitute for reviewable row outcomes.
sources.evidence_limitations: No PostgreSQL backend was supplied; conversion-error handling does not define application identity, business validation, or all structural CSV errors.
